subject: Licensing model & environment count — VPC pilot follow-up
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Licensing model & environment count — VPC pilot follow-up

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a few asks so we can turn the call into a scoped pilot quote: 

Recap from our discovery call:
- Primary use case: customer-facing conversational assistants for support and internal knowledge search.
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: you indicated a range (30M–50M/mo) with weekday peaks on launch days.
- Peak concurrency: ~40 concurrent sessions (50–60 session windows/day).
- Data isolation requirement: VPC with private control plane, SOC2 evidence and audit logs required.

Items we need to finalize to prepare a formal pilot quote:
1) Confirm expected environment count — do you want separate prod / staging / dev (3), or are you planning additional DR or sandbox envs?
2) Budget range target for the pilot (monthly) and any hard cap. You mentioned a ballpark earlier, confirming helps us choose model.
3) Preferred support tier: Standard (business hours) or Enterprise (24/7 SLA + named engineer)?
4) Target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for in the pricing conversation — that lets us size committed vs metered options.

High-level licensing options we plan to quote (attached: redwood_vpc_pricing_options_v1.pdf):
- Option A — Reserved Environments: fixed monthly license per environment + included token bucket. Good for predictable throughput.
- Option B — Metered + Base Fee: lower base fee, pay per 1M tokens above an included baseline. Good for variable usage.
- Add-ons: enterprise support, extended retention, dedicated deployment windowing, and on-prem deployment add-on.

If you can reply with answers to the four bullets above, we will put together two candidate pilots (30-day and 90-day) with unit economics and an MRP line for procurement.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_pricing_options_v1.pdf (pricing summary)

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and will loop in engineering for any technical follow-ups once we lock env counts.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Licensing model & environment count — VPC pilot follow-up

Thanks Nikhil — appreciated the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Monthly token estimate: closer to 35M–45M/mo to start (we expect upticks with marketing pushes), so please size around 40M/mo as a working number.
- Environments: we need prod + staging + dev + a sandbox for partners = 4 environments.
- Support: enterprise tier preferred given SLAs and compliance needs.
- Budget: procurement asked us to target ~$8k–$15k/month for the pilot (including support). Final PO will depend on the quote breakdown (license + tokens + support).
- Timeline: procurement prefers a 90-day pilot but open to a 30-day technical evaluation first.

I attached our SOW / procurement checklist so you can see the procurement timelines and required fields.

Attachments: Acme_SOW_requirements.pdf

Subject: Re: Licensing model & environment count — VPC pilot follow-up

Liam — thanks for the quick reply and the SOW. Based on your answers (4 envs, enterprise support, target pilot budget $8k–$15k/mo), we put together two candidate pilots. High-level economics below; I attached a mutual action plan we can convert to a PO-friendly quote.

Pilot A — 30-day technical evaluation (smaller footprint)
- Environments: 2 (prod, staging) with sandbox access for test traffic
- Token baseline: 10M included tokens; overage at $950 / 1M tokens
- License: $3,000 / env / month (dedicated VPC env licensing) — includes private control plane and audit logs
- Support: Enterprise lite (extended hours, named AM): $2,500/mo
- Estimated total (baseline): $3,000*2 + $2,500 + overage (if 40M projected -> +30M extra = $28,500 at $950/1M) — this is likely above your target for a short eval, so this option is best for technical validation only.

Pilot B — 90-day pilot (production-like, committed bucket)
- Environments: 4 (prod, staging, dev, partner sandbox)
- Committed token bucket: 40M / month included
- License: $2,200 / env / month (volume-discounted for commitment)
- Token overage: $700 / 1M tokens above committed bucket
- Support: Enterprise (24/7 SLA + named engineer): $5,000 / month included
- Estimated total (baseline): $2,200*4 + $5,000 = $13,800 / month (includes 40M tokens).
  - Unit economics note: if you use the full 40M tokens, effective $/1M tokens is ~ $345 (license amortized across included tokens). If you go above 40M, overage steps in at $700 / 1M.

Recommendation and next steps:
- Given procurement preference for a 90-day pilot and your compliance needs, Pilot B is the most likely to fit both cost and operational needs. It stays in your $8k–$15k target at the lower end of list price; if you confirm a firm 12–18 month commitment we can reduce the per-env license and lower overage to $600 / 1M.
- Please confirm: 1) final approval for 4 environments, 2) whether procurement needs an MSA + PO before pilot start, and 3) preferred pilot start date (you mentioned mid-September).

Attachments: pilot_mutual_action_plan.docx

Ben — tagging you for any commercial tweaks before I send the formal quote to procurement.

Subject: Re: Licensing model & environment count — VPC pilot follow-up

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Nikhil. Pilot B looks sensible — confirms our procurement and product alignment.

- Environment count: confirmed 4.
- Support: Enterprise confirmed.
- Pilot term: we prefer a 90-day pilot with a target start date of 2026-09-15.
- Budget: our internal target is ~$12,000 / month (we can stretch within your $8k–$15k band but we need a clear per-month cap for PO).

Next asks from our side so procurement can issue a PO:
1) Finalized quote with line items (license by env, included tokens, support fee, any one-time onboarding)
2) Standard MSA or Data Processing Addendum if available — procurement prefers early review.
3) Simple acceptance criteria for the 90-day pilot (uptime, latency targets, data handling).

If you can get a formal quote and MSA over by next Wednesday (2026-09-01) we can route it through procurement and target 9/15 start.

Thanks — Liam
